text:
maya: Quick follow-up from the RFC meeting — we need a short plan for how the runtime will decide between FP8/INT8/4-bit on a per-request basis. main constraints: quality degradation detection, KV cache compatibility, and rollback safety.

samir: can we rely solely on degscore telemetry to gate switches? that's what we've been leaning on in evals.

olivia: degscore is necessary but not sufficient. it misses locale/format hallucinations. we should also track CONTRAST-F1 on a small prompt set per-customer and token-level perplexity drift.

kevin: runtime concerns: switching precision mid-session breaks KV cache layout. either we keep a single canonical cache format or add compatibility shims. both have perf/cost tradeoffs.

maya: agreed. proposal A: enforce precision at session start (fast, simple), with auto-fallback to compatible model variant when quality triggers. Proposal B: add adapter layer to translate KV cache across precisions (byteswap + re-quantize) — slower but enables mid-session adaptivity.

jin: +1 for option A for initial rollout. cheaper to implement and simpler for canaries. we should document the exact fallback chain: FP8 -> INT8 -> 4bit? or FP8 -> 4bit -> INT8?

leah: ordering depends on model-specific degradation curves. for some Llama variants INT8 has better quality than naive 4bit. we should make ordering part of the quant-profile metadata: e.g. "fallback_order": ["fp8", "int8", "4bit"].

kevin: runtime needs to read that metadata and pick the first available slot with capacity. also need to ensure billing+metrics map to the effective precision. 

maya: decision for now: implement session-level precision pins + per-endpoint quant-profile metadata that lists fallback_order and safe-token-limits. canary plan: 1) add `quant_profile` field to model manifest, 2) enforce session pin in runtime codepath, 3) enable degscore and contrast-f1 eval hooks before and after canary, 4) rollback rule: if degscore delta > 0.05 or contrast-f1 drop > 3 points, auto-failover to previous profile.

olivia: add test plan: small A/B with 10k requests across 5 customer prompt sets, measure: degscore, contrast-f1, latency p95, token-cost.

samir: ops ask: how will on-call get alerted? we should emit a structured event `quant-profile-degradation` with fields: profile_id, model, delta_deg, delta_contrast, affected_sessions (estimate). tanya-bot can trigger a page if delta_deg>0.1.

maya: good. action items: @jin please spike session-pin implementation (runtime) — 2w. @leah please draft quant_profile schema PR with fallback_order and safe_token_limits — 3d. @olivia + @samir design the eval harness and alert thresholds — 1w. I'll own canary run coordination and docs.

kevin: one more note — KV cache migration work should be a separate RFC. we can keep it off the L2 rollout to reduce scope.

maya: thanks everyone. I'll summarize and open a follow-up doc with the exact manifest fields and canary checklist. :thumbsup:
